output.name: Hannel

anatomy.part: left end of the loom beam, the bar the warp is strung from
right end of the loom beam, the hook where the cord is tied
neck of the weight, where the cord meets the stone

output.myth: When Aun cut the string the sky ran up so fast the year's sailcloth nearly tore from the Reel. Hesk was quick. She reached down with her long hands and hung a weight on the Lamp Road, a grey stone with a hole through it, tied to a cord of goat-gut and fixed to the beam of the sky. Hannel does not sing or sleep. Its work is to keep the warp straight so the year can be woven without a snag. Every winter Tavo comes down the cord and shakes it, laughing, to see whether it will swing. Sil watches from the drowned lantern of her face, and when the moon is thin she says it is still hanging. Ennu says that is all a good weight ever does. My mother's mother said that the day Hannel swings, every sail we own will split along its seams, and the Gulls will come down to pick up the pieces. So mind your knots, child, and count your stitches.
output.verse:
A stone on a cord
it hangs from the Road's long beam
keep the sail-year taut
